sentences.text: Chaoyangopterus possessed a toothless skull measuring approximately 270 mm in length and an estimated wingspan of 1.85 meters.

Fossils of this pterosaur were discovered in the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation near Chaoyang, Liaoning, China, and the genus was named and described in 2003 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.
The species name 'zhangi' honors journalist Zhang Wanlian for his work protecting fossil sites.
Wang originally assumed the toothless Chaoyangopterus was a fish-eater, though its full paleobiology remains undetailed.
The original describers classified Chaoyangopterus as a nyctosaurid, noting it was most similar to Nyctosaurus.
David Unwin classified Chaoyangopterus within the Tapejaridae family, a group of azhdarchoids known for large head crests.
A 2006 analysis by Lü Junchang and Ji Qiang identified Chaoyangopterus as a basal azhdarchoid without specific familial affiliation.
Later analysis by Lü and Unwin placed Chaoyangopterus in the family Chaoyangopteridae, a clade including Jidapterus and Shenzhoupterus.
In 2006, Wang and Zhou argued that Chaoyangopterus belonged to the Pteranodontidae family and that other genera were junior synonyms.
A 2017 redescription of Jidapterus refuted the claim that Chaoyangopterus and related genera were synonyms.
A 2011 study by Pinheiro et al. placed Chaoyangopterus in the subfamily Chaoyangopterinae within the family Tapejaridae.
Chaoyangopterus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
